title: Enterprise LLM Customization Path (Prompt+RAG vs SFT/Multi-LoRA vs Distillation) & Cloud GPU SKU Sizing

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Blind Full-Weight Fine-Tuning (`70B SFT`) for Dynamic Enterprise Knowledge
tiers.architecture: Baking daily-changing enterprise facts into 70B full-parameter weights + deploying 20 separate 70B GPU clusters for 20 business units

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Giant Few-Shot Prompt + RAG on Frontier/70B Model Only (No SFT or Distillation)
tiers.architecture: Stuffing 6,000 tokens of few-shot style/schema examples + 4,000 RAG tokens into every 70B call

tiers.tier: Tier 3: RAG + Multi-LoRA `vLLM / SGLang` Shared Base Model (`1x 70B Base + 20 Hot-Swapped LoRA Adapters`)
tiers.architecture: RAG for dynamic knowledge + rank-32 LoRA SFT for domain schema/tone served from a single shared 70B H200/H100 pool
tiers.required_gpu_fleet_footprint: 8x H200 (141GB) or 12x H100 (80GB) shared Multi-LoRA pool

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Hybrid RAG + Task-Distilled `8B` Student on `L40S` (80% Traffic) + Shared `70B Multi-LoRA` on `H200` (20% Hard Traffic)
tiers.architecture: Distill 70B teacher traces into a specialized 8B FP8 model on cost-effective L40S GPUs for 80% routine tasks + RAG + 70B Multi-LoRA on H200 for 20% complex reasoning
tiers.required_gpu_fleet_footprint: 8x L40S (48GB) for 8B Student + 4x H200 (141GB) for 70B Multi-LoRA

scenarios.scenario: The #1 Enterprise Myth: 'Let's Fine-Tune a Model on Our Company PDFs So It Knows Our Products'
scenarios.question: A VP of Engineering wants to run SFT on 50,000 internal product manuals and daily price sheets instead of building RAG
scenarios.model_answer: Use the Orthogonal Customization Law: **RAG is for dynamic facts, citations, and access control (`ACL`); SFT/LoRA is for output format, domain syntax, tone, and压缩 6,000-token few-shot examples into weights!** Combining RAG + LoRA reaches 96.6% accuracy vs 62.4% for SFT-only (which hallucinates stale prices and cannot enforce per-user document ACLs)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 full-weight SFT forgets yesterday's price updates, hallucinates citations, and leaks restricted training facts to unauthorized users (62.4% accuracy).

scenarios.scenario: Serving 20 Business-Unit Custom Models Without Buying 20 Separate GPU Clusters (`Multi-LoRA`)
scenarios.question: 20 enterprise departments (Legal, HR, Tax, Claims, etc.) each fine-tune a custom 70B adapter; deploying 20 dedicated 70B clusters costs $245K/month
scenarios.model_answer: Deploy a single shared `70B FP8` base model on `vLLM / SGLang` with Dynamic Multi-LoRA batching (`S-LoRA / Punica` kernels): 20 rank-32 LoRA adapters (~160 MB each) co-reside in HBM/RAM and execute in the same continuous batch, cutting GPU count from 64x H100 to 8x H200 ($54K/mo)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 deploys isolated GPU nodes per fine-tuned checkpoint, leaving 18 of 20 departmental clusters sitting at <10% utilization.

scenarios.scenario: When to Distill a 70B/Frontier Teacher into an 8B Student on `L40S` GPUs (`Teacher -> Student Distillation`)
scenarios.question: 80% of production traffic consists of repetitive high-volume tasks (ticket classification, JSON entity extraction, SQL dialect translation) running at 250 QPS
scenarios.model_answer: Harvest 20,000 verified gold traces from the 70B/GPT-4o Teacher and fine-tune/distill an `8B FP8` Student (`Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen2.5-7B`) deployed on `NVIDIA L40S (48GB)` GPUs: eliminates 5,000 tokens of few-shot prompt bloat, cuts P99 latency from 1,820ms to 245ms, and reduces monthly TCO to $28.5K (-88.4%)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 pays frontier/70B compute and 6,000-token few-shot prefill cost on every single routine extraction call ($142K/mo).

scenarios.scenario: Cloud GPU SKU Selection Matrix (`H200 141GB` vs. `H100 80GB` vs. `A100 80GB` vs. `L40S 48GB`)
scenarios.question: How should an architect map `8B`, `32B`, and `70B+` models across `L40S`, `A100`, `H100`, and `H200` instances?
scenarios.model_answer: Map by Memory Capacity (`VRAM`) and Bandwidth (`TB/s`): (1) `8B–14B FP8` (`<= 16K` ctx) -> **1x L40S 48GB** (`864 GB/s`, best $/tok for small models); (2) `70B FP8` standard context -> **2x H100 80GB** (`3.35 TB/s` + native FP8); (3) `70B FP8` long-context (`32K–128K`) or high-batch Multi-LoRA -> **1x–2x H200 141GB** (`4.8 TB/s`, holds 72GB weights + 60GB KV cache on a single GPU without TP=2 cross-card overhead!)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Running 70B models on A10G/L40S (requires 4-card PCIe tensor parallelism with severe communication bottlenecks) or running 8B models on expensive H100s at low batch sizes.

perturbation_checks.check: 6,000-Token Few-Shot Prompt Compression via LoRA SFT (`6,000 Input Tokens -> 400 Input Tokens`)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 245ms P99 Latency | $28.5K/mo (93% Prefill Token Reduction via Weight Internalization)

perturbation_checks.check: Single-GPU `H200 (141GB)` vs. Dual-GPU `2x H100 (80GB)` for 70B FP8 Serving
perturbation_checks.original: 2x H100 TP=2 (160GB VRAM, NVLink AllReduce Overhead)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 1x H200 TP=1 (141GB HBM3e @ 4.8 TB/s -> Zero Cross-GPU TP Overhead, +28% Tokens/s per GPU)

key_findings: Tier 4 (RAG for dynamic facts + Distilled 8B Student on L40S for 80% routine traffic + Shared 70B Multi-LoRA on H200 for 20% complex traffic) achieves 96.6% domain accuracy, 99.1% schema adherence, 245ms P99 latency, and $28,500/mo TCO (-88.4% vs isolated 70B SFT clusters).

RAG and Fine-Tuning are orthogonal, not substitutes: use RAG for changing knowledge and per-user ACLs; use LoRA SFT/Distillation to lock in output schema, domain syntax, and eliminate 6,000-token few-shot prompt bloat.
Right-sizing GPU SKUs by memory capacity and FP8 support (`L40S 48GB` for 8B–14B, `H200 141GB` single-GPU for 70B FP8 + large KV cache) boosts throughput per dollar by 2.4x–3.8x.
